findings.description: The bucket is explicitly noted and configured as public with no ACL restriction, allowing unauthenticated or unintended access to potentially sensitive customer data stored within it (customer-master.xlsx).
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects stored in this bucket are not encrypted at rest, risking exposure of sensitive data if the underlying storage is compromised.
Versioning is not enabled, meaning objects (including sensitive customer master data) can be overwritten or deleted without recovery, increasing risk from accidental or malicious data loss/tampering.
A sensitive file (customer-master.xlsx) is uploaded into the aws_s3_bucket.data bucket, which is public and unencrypted, directly exposing customer data to unauthorized access.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket holding financial data, leaving stored objects unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, leaving stored objects unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, leaving stored objects unencrypted at rest despite having logging and versioning enabled.
